producer_report.summary:
Root cause: the scope guard learned why an attempt stopped from a free-text closing-reason prefix, and two lists of 'environment' reasons disagreed. The guard used its own `environment:` prefix, while `disk::is_environment_reason` listed only low disk and a check timeout. A producer that died on an expired login (API error 401) was closed as 'the producer did not complete: ...', which matched neither list. It counted as line spend, raised T1/T3/T5 and paused the line, and no one rechecked the stored pause.

Fix:
- `disk.rs` now holds one classifier, `StopCause::of`. It also has `producer_stop_reason` and a narrow parser, `api_error_status`, that accepts only the CLI's 'API Error: <status>' form (401 is auth, 429 is usage limit), with subtype success or error. `is_environment_reason` and `resumable_stop` use it.
- `scope_guard.rs` drops its own prefix. A new `verdict_of` uses the classifier, and only a job closed `failed` can be an environment attempt, so TimedOut producer stops still count as work.
- `producer.rs` closes API-error producer stops with the environment reason.
- `line_pause` now recomputes the signals from the line's attempts and returns the stored pause only while it still reaches a pause. It never creates one, and the file is left as it is.
- The forecast for that recompute comes from the newest request with a finished attempt (`line_forecast_p90`). The watcher uses the same function, so a request joining the line cannot drop a T3 pause.
- `athena status` uses `live_marks`, so stale marks are hidden.
- CHANGELOG has an Unreleased entry.

Tests cover the expired-login line, every environment kind, work-failure controls, the state gate, stale versus real pauses, status filtering, a T3 pause after a request joins the line, and resumability. The expired-login detail is built through the real `StreamState::on_line` and `output_from_result`.

fmt, clippy, the policy scan and the full test suite all pass.

`run/mod.rs` needed no change: `settle_resume_marks` already calls `is_environment_reason`, so it picks up the new classifier.

I did not revert the change to watch the new tests fail.

Open: the 401 JSON shape comes from the brief, not a stored sample. Usage limits are recognized only as 'API Error: 429'.

The CHANGELOG sentence 'The pause file is left as it is' also holds for status: it only hides stale marks.

No governance file was edited."

checks_run.command: cargo test -p athena-core scope_guard (run with the disk filter in one command)
checks_run.note: all new and existing scope_guard and disk tests passed after two test fixes
whole workspace passed, including 732 athena-core lib tests (1 ignored before the change too)

criteria_check.criterion: The change description names the root cause: the guard infers the stop reason from free-text closing-reason prefixes and has two disagreeing environment lists, so an auth-expiry stop counted as line spend; the fix is in the shared classifier in crates/athena-core/src/disk.rs and scope_guard.rs, not in one job's data.
criteria_check.evidence: The `StopCause` doc comment in disk.rs, the scope_guard.rs module doc and the CHANGELOG.md Unreleased entry each name it. The fix is `disk::StopCause::of` and `producer_stop_reason`, used by `scope_guard::verdict_of`. No job data is touched.

criteria_check.criterion: `scope_guard::attempt_of` and `disk::is_environment_reason`/`resumable_stop` use one classifier (no second hard-coded list); Grep shows a single definition of which closing reasons are environment stops.
criteria_check.evidence: `attempt_of` calls `verdict_of`, which calls `disk::is_environment_reason`, which is `StopCause::of(..).is_environment()`; `resumable_stop` calls `is_environment_reason`. Grep of ENVIRONMENT_PREFIX and starts_with("environment under crates/ finds the definition and its use only in disk.rs. Test `disk::tests::one_classifier_decides_environment_reasons` passes.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-core scope_guard`: a new test builds a line of several attempts that all closed with the producer-auth-expired reason (the 'the producer did not complete: ... 401 OAuth access token has expired' text) and asserts T1, T3 and T5 give Level::None; the same test fails when the classifier change is reverted. A second test covers each environment reason kind (low disk, check timeout, auth, usage limit), not one job's text.
criteria_check.evidence: `scope_guard::tests::a_line_of_expired_login_stops_raises_no_signal` builds four attempts (40 min, $0.60 each) from three constructions of the 401 reason (new form, stored form, literal) and asserts t1, t3, t5 and overall are None. `the_same_line_closed_for_a_failure_of_the_work_does_raise_signals` shows the same attempts give T1 Flag, T3 Flag and T5 Pause under a work-failure reason. Before the change a 401 reason would not match the old prefix and would map to Failed. `every_kind_of_environment_stop_is_an_environment_attempt` covers low disk, check timeout, auth, usage limit and an unknown environment: reason. The run passed. I did not revert the change to watch the test fail.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-core scope_guard`: a test shows a stored pause whose signals no longer hold under the current attempts is not returned by `line_pause` (the pause is recomputed from attempts), while a pause for real repeated rejections still is.
criteria_check.evidence: `watcher_tests::a_stored_pause_that_no_longer_holds_is_not_returned_and_does_not_block_a_retry` writes a T4 pause on a line with two different-criterion rejections. `line_pause` returns None, the file stays and `retry` is not refused. The control line with two same-criterion rejections returns the pause and refuses the retry. `a_t3_pause_still_holds_after_a_new_request_joins_the_line` and the reworked `retry_refuses_paused_line` also pass. `status_shows_only_the_marks_that_still_hold` passes.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-core disk`: a producer stop on an expired login is a resumable stop, so `athena retry` can resume it.
criteria_check.evidence: `disk::tests::a_producer_stop_on_an_expired_login_is_resumable` passes: `resumable_stop(Closed(Failed), ..)` is true for the stored form and the new form, with the detail built through StreamState::on_line and output_from_result. It is false for error_max_turns text, no valid report, and Rejected, Landed and TimedOut states.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test`: all pass.
criteria_check.evidence: left to Athena's checks. I ran fmt --all, clippy --all-targets --locked -D warnings and cargo test --locked --quiet; all passed.

criteria_check.criterion: CHANGELOG.md is not required; no existing reading rule, athena.toml, defaults.toml or workflow changes (git diff shows none).
criteria_check.evidence: Edited files: crates/athena-core/src/disk.rs, scope_guard.rs, run/producer.rs, status.rs and CHANGELOG.md (an added entry). No athena.toml, defaults.toml, workflow or reading rule was touched.

open_issues: The expired-login JSON shape (subtype success, is_error true, text 'Failed to authenticate. API Error: 401 ...') is taken from the brief, not from a stored record. If a real sample has another lead-in, `disk::api_error_status` must accept it.
The usage-limit stop is recognized only as 'API Error: 429'. A usage-limit stop in another text form still counts as work until a sample is found.
TimedOut producer stops still count as work spend. That is a different cause and I left it.

An environment-stopped attempt that a later attempt redid from scratch still counts toward T3 spend (existing rule in `t3_basis`). For an auth stop the real cost is near zero, so this rarely matters, and the test keeps its costs realistic.
A follow-up could carry the API-error status on AgentOutput instead of re-parsing the detail text.
mistakes: My first draft of the T3 test assumed the joining request had no reading; the rig gives it one, and the test failed. I fixed it by clearing the readings on the records.
The first draft of the work-failure test asserted `api_error_status` was None for 'API Error: 500'; it returns Some(500). I changed the assertion to 'not 401 or 429'.
The first full `cargo test --locked` output was too large to read back. I reran it with --quiet, and it passed.
learnings: Rig `ask` runs a reading, so a request that joins a line already carries a reading in the fake rig. A test of the reading-less case clears `readings` on the records it passes to `line_pause`.

`t3_basis` keeps the spend of an environment-stopped attempt when a later attempt redid the work from scratch. So the cost in the expired-login test is kept under the flag threshold: three counted attempts of $0.60 stay below a $2.00 p90. This is existing behavior and I did not change it.
The Grep tool and Bash pipes cannot read saved tool-output files outside the working directory; rerun cargo with --quiet to get short output.
desires: A real sample of the CLI's JSON for an expired-login result and a usage-limit result, to fix the exact lead-in text the parser accepts.
A way to read the saved cargo output file, which the Grep tool refused because it sits outside the working directory.
